Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 23-Nov-2025 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  FIFTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  Advanced Data Structure [DS_5025]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                       Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Derive the worst-case time complexity of the Manipal function                                           (5)  
  void Manipal(int n) {  
  $$A)           int i = 1;$$  
  while (i < n) {  
  $$for (int j = 0; j < i; j++) {$$  
  printf("%d ", j);  
  }  
  $$i *= 2;$$  
  }  
  }  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Use the recursive tree method to solve the recurrence T(n) = 2T(n/2) + cn and find its time             (5)  
  complexity.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2)                Given the following array of numbers                                                                    (5)  
  38, 27, 43, 3, 9, 82, 10  
  A)  
  Sort the numbers using a divide-and-conquer-based Sorting algorithm with O(nLogn) worst-case  
  time complexity. Write the Pseudocode for the algorithm.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           You are given the following sequence of integers to insert into an initially empty AVL Tree             (5)  
  50, 30, 70, 20, 40, 60, 80, 10, 35, 45  
  
  Insert the nodes one by one into the AVL Tree.  
  After each insertion, perform necessary rotations to maintain AVL balance.  
  Draw the final AVL Tree structure.  
  Mention the balance factor of each node in the final tree.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3)                Given a chain of matrix                                                                                 (5)  
  A1: 5X4  
  A2: 4X3  
  Page #1

A)          A4: 5X2  
  A3: 3X5  
  A5: 2X4  
  
  where Ai has dimensions pi-1 x pi. Fully parenthesize the product A1 .A2 . .... A5 in a way that  
  minimizes the number of scalar multiplications.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)          Given an array consisting of the following elements: {-2, -5, 6, -2, -3, 1, 5, -6}. Find a contiguous (5)  
  non-empty subarray within the array that has the maximum sum, and return the sum as well as the  
  subarray elements. Implement using an appropriate design paradigm, give the optimized algorithm,  
  and derive the time complexity.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4)               Differentiate between FIFO and LIFO batch and bound methods for the following 0/1 knapsack            (5)  
  problem, where the knapsack capacity is 15kg.  
  A)  
  
  
  Illustrate the FIFO and LIFO-based knapsack solution trees.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)          Use a Multiobjective Genetic Algorithm to solve a problem with two conflicting objectives. Apply      (5)  
  Pareto optimality to select the best solutions from the population.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5)               Use a polynomial-time reduction to show that a given problem is NP-complete. Apply the two NP- (5)  
  completeness conditions and demonstrate the process using a known NP-complete problem as the  
  A)          basis for reduction.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)          Perform a polynomial-time reduction from the 3-SAT problem to the Clique problem. Apply the           (5)  
  transformation to a sample 3-SAT instance and construct the corresponding graph to demonstrate  
  how satisfiability is preserved."  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"
